articles.standfirst: La Selección ha encajado gol en todos los partidos de la Nations League cuando apenas recibió uno en todo el Mundial
articles.summary: La Selección ha encajado gol en todos los partidos de la Nations League cuando apenas recibió uno en todo el Mundial
articles.body: De un tiempo a esta parte, España está desplegando un nivel de fútbol prácticamente impecable. La racha de partidos sin perder ya supera los 40 y no parece tener un final cercano. Sin embargo, hay un pequeño detalle que no le está permitiendo alcanzar la excelencia en esta Nations League: la fragilidad defensiva. La Selección ha encajado en los tres partidos que ha disputado hasta ahora y se ha acostumbrado a conceder un gol que durante el pasado Mundial fue prácticamente una excepción. Sin necesidad de encerrarse atrás ni mucho menos, la fortaleza defensiva fue uno de los grandes avales de España para conquistar el Mundial. Tan sólo Bélgica, en los cuartos de final, consiguió marcarle durante todo el torneo. Por eso llama especialmente la atención el contraste con esta Nations League, donde Inglaterra, Croacia y República Checa ya han encontrado la manera de superar a la defensa española. Lo más importante es que esas concesiones no han tenido consecuencias: la Selección cuenta sus partidos por victorias y lidera el grupo en solitario. Ante Croacia, el reto será dejar sellada la clasificación para los cuartos de final y, de paso, volver a ponerle el candado a la portería. Las apuestas deportivas de Tonybet reflejan esa posibilidad y sitúan en 1.93 la cuota a que ambos equipos no vean portería. España ha demostrado que no necesita mantener su portería a cero para ganar, pero recuperar esa solidez defensiva supondría una señal especialmente positiva de cara a las próximas eliminatorias. En cualquier caso, se espera un partido con alternativas y con posibilidades de que el marcador vuelva a dispararse. Los tres encuentros que han disputado Croacia y España en esta Nations League han superado la línea de 2.5 goles totales. El último precedente entre ambas selecciones, disputado hace apenas una semana en el Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán, terminó con cinco tantos. Las mejores casas de apuestas también contemplan un escenario de goles: Tonybet paga a 3.35 que vuelvan a marcarse más de 2.5 en Split. España afronta así un nuevo examen después de haber demostrado que puede ganar, incluso, cuando deja algún resquicio atrás. Pero el objetivo ante Croacia va más allá de conseguir otra victoria: también pasa por recuperar una de las señas de identidad que la llevaron a conquistar el Mundial. Tonybet pone precio tanto a la posibilidad de un partido sin goles en ambas porterías como a un nuevo festival ofensivo. Esta vez, la Selección espera que, si vuelven a caer goles, todos sean de su lado... y que la puerta quede finalmente cerrada. articles.title: El anuncio de Pedro Sánchez da el varapalo definitivo a la rebaja de la tasa de alcohol al volante
articles.standfirst: El objetivo de poder rebajar los límites ha vuelto a alejarse tras la disolución de las Cortes y el anuncio de las próximas elecciones generales
articles.summary: No está teniendo el viento de cara la DGT para sacar adelante su plan de rebajar los límites máximos de alcoholemia al volante.
articles.body: No está teniendo el viento de cara la DGT para sacar adelante su plan de rebajar los límites máximos de alcoholemia al volante. Recordemos que el objetivo del equipo de Pere Navarro pasaba por rebajar el actual límite de 0,25 miligramos/litro en aire espirado a solo 0,1, lo que equivale a pasar de 0,5 g/litro en sangre a 0,2. El objetivo, reconocido por la propia DGT, sigue siendo conseguir que los conductores no prueben el alcohol antes de ponerse al volante, porque estos límites propuestos, en la práctica, equivalen a no haber bebido. La nueva propuesta haría que la mayoría de los conductores estuvieran en el límite de dar positivo tomando una caña o media copa de vino. Con un botellín de cerveza o una copa de vino la multa merecería la consideración de "Grave" (entre 0,1 y 0,25 mg/litro en aire espirado, con pérdida de dos puntos y pago de 200 euros). Con dos tercios o dos copas de vino sería infracción "Muy grave" (de 0,26 a 0,5 mg/l en aire, con cuatro puntos y 500 euros). Y en casos de cuatro o cinco tercios, o una botella de vino, la infracción sería "muy grave" (1.000 euros de multa y 6 puntos del carné por superar los 0,5 mg/litro en aire). En marzo el plan fue rechazado en el Congreso de los Diputados con los votos en contra de PP, Vox y ERC, pero el 30 de enero la propuesta fue admitida de nuevo a trámite en la Cámara Baja en un proceso que podría haber hecho posible que entrara en vigor antes de verano de 2027. Sin embargo, todo el proceso que podía haber hecho que esta nueva norma fuera una realidad ha quedado paralizada tras la disolución de las cámaras y el anuncio de una próxima convocatoria de elecciones generales por parte de Pedro Sánchez. Y es de prever que no salga adelante con un hipotético gobierno central de PP y Vox, que ya se han manifestado en contra de este cambio. En la actualidad, los países de la Unión Europea en los que no está admitido nada de alcohol al volante son República Checa, Eslovaquia, Hungría y Rumanía, mientras que Estonia, Polonia, Suecia y Lituania ya tienen el límite máximo permitido de 0,10 mg/l en aire que deseaba implantar el ejecutivo.

articles.title: Exploring Sloane Stephens and Jozy Altidore’s love story that took years to build before their marriage came to an end
articles.summary: Sloane Stephens and Jozy Altidore’s relationship began long before they became a famous sports couple. The tennis star and former U.S.
articles.body: Sloane Stephens and Jozy Altidore’s relationship began long before they became a famous sports couple. The tennis star and former U.S. soccer international first met as children in Florida before losing touch as their sporting careers took them in different directions. Years later, they unexpectedly reunited and turned their childhood connection into a serious relationship, eventually getting married in 2022.Their marriage, however, came to an end four years later. Stephens announced their separation in February 2026, saying they had decided to end their marriage while asking for privacy.Inside Sloane Stephens and Jozy Altidore’s love story Sloane Stephens and Jozy Altidore first knew each other while attending Boca Prep International School in Florida. Stephens was in fifth grade, while Altidore was two grades ahead. Their childhood friendship eventually faded as both pursued successful careers in professional sports.The two reunited in 2016 at the Home Depot Center in Carson, California. Altidore was attending a U.S. men’s national team camp, while Stephens was training for the Fed Cup. Their unexpected meeting quickly brought their old connection back.“I was doing a media scrum in the hallway during a U.S. Men’s National team camp. Sloane was there training for Fed Cup in Hawaii,” Altidore previously told Vogue of their reunion. “Sloane turned the corner while having a loud conversation on FaceTime. We locked eyes and started talking during the scrum.”The pair exchanged numbers and later went to dinner after one of Altidore’s games.Their relationship eventually led to an emotional proposal in April 2019. Altidore surprised Stephens at an art gallery in Los Angeles. Instead of paintings, the space was filled with huge photographs celebrating their relationship and the people closest to Stephens.The couple later announced their engagement on social media.They married on January 1, 2022, at the St. Regis Bal Harbour in Miami Beach. Their wedding carried strong family significance. Stephens had lost both grandparents in the same week in 2021. She honoured their memory by wrapping their handkerchiefs around her bridal bouquet.Since they split due to growing apart over time, Stephens has appeared determined to move forward. During a recent Instagram Q&A, she described herself as happy and focused on enjoying the present.“Yes! Absolutely life maxing right now. Living for now, saying yes to more, making the memories, and enjoying every moment as it comes. Life moves fast and I don’t want to miss the good parts waiting for the “right” time,” she posted.Her focus has also returned to tennis. Stephens recently reached the quarterfinals of the Guadalajara Open. She later explained that her ranking had limited her opportunities during the Asian swing.She is now preparing for tournaments in Edmond, Oklahoma, and New Braunfels, Texas, as she looks to improve her ranking before the end of the year.Jozy Altidore, meanwhile, was last seen on field during the New England Revolution’s Major League Soccer (MLS) win over Inter Miami CF.From childhood friends to married partners and now separate paths, Stephens and Altidore’s story has gone through several chapters. articles.title: Néstor Lorenzo reconoce las dificultades en el proceso de recambio de la Selección Colombia
articles.standfirst: La sincera confesión de Néstor Lorenzo sobre el cambio generacional en Colombia
articles.summary: La sincera confesión de Néstor Lorenzo sobre el cambio generacional en Colombia
articles.body: La fecha FIFA de octubre deja reflexiones profundas en el seno de la Selección Colombia. Tras los recientes ensayos frente a rivales continentales como Paraguay y México, el director técnico Néstor Lorenzo fue autocrítico y abordó abiertamente la complejidad que implica llevar a cabo el recambio generacional del equipo de cara al ciclo de la Copa América 2028 y el Mundial 2030. Tras la ratificación de su contrato por parte de la Federación Colombiana de Fútbol, el estratega argentino ha iniciado una etapa de prueba e integración de nuevas caras en la 'Tricolor'. Nombres como Aldair Quintana, Kevin Andrade, Édier Ocampo, Camilo Durán y Álvaro Angulo han sumado sus primeros minutos, mientras otros jóvenes talentos como Yáser Asprilla o Juan Manuel Rengifo buscan consolidarse en la dinámica de la Selección. Sin embargo, Lorenzo reconoció que este proceso de integración dista de ser sencillo: "Es muy difícil encontrar un buen funcionamiento con jugadores nuevos en tan poco tiempo. Estamos en construcción y es más difícil, sobre todo si el resultado no te ayuda. Tenemos que pensar en lo que individualmente cada jugador nos está dando y lo que pueden aportar en el futuro", explicó el DT. Más allá de la rotación de nombres, el entrenador probó variaciones tácticas significativas —como el ajuste a una línea de tres defensores frente a Paraguay— que dejaron al descubierto dificultades en la elaboración de juego, la salida limpia desde el fondo y la contundencia en el área rival. El debate actual no gira alrededor de una sustitución drástica de la nómina, sino de una transición progresiva. La base del equipo mantendrá referentes de experiencia que ayuden a sostener la competitividad mientras los nuevos convocados asimilan la idea de juego. El margen de ensayo es reducido en el fútbol de selecciones, y Néstor Lorenzo es consciente de ello: la urgencia de cosechar resultados inmediatos a menudo condiciona la paciencia que requiere la formación de una nueva identidad colectiva. Los amistosos continúan siendo la principal plataforma para sacar conclusiones individuales y grupales en la búsqueda del equipo ideal.

articles.title: Shakira y Dua Lipa cantan juntas ‘Antología’ en Madrid y rompen récord de audiencia histórico
articles.standfirst: Inolvidable: Shakira y Dua Lipa paralizan Madrid cantando a dúo ‘Antología’ y marcan un récord histórico
articles.summary: Inolvidable: Shakira y Dua Lipa paralizan Madrid cantando a dúo ‘Antología’ y marcan un récord histórico
articles.body: Un encuentro imprevisto entre dos de las figuras más influyentes del pop global paralizó las redes sociales y las plataformas de transmisión en vivo. Durante la octava fecha de la residencia de Shakira en la capital española —en el marco de su gira Las Mujeres Ya No Lloran World Tour—, la cantante británica Dua Lipa apareció por sorpresa en el escenario para interpretar a dúo el emblemático tema "Antología". El show contó con transmisión en directo global a través de Amazon Music, congregando a más de 10 millones de usuarios conectados simultáneamente. Esta cifra convirtió al evento en la presentación femenina en vivo más vista en la historia de la plataforma. El dueto no fue fruto del azar. La relación entre Dua Lipa y este clásico de 1995 (lanzado originalmente en el álbum Pies descalzos) se gestó meses atrás: Antes de dar paso al tema, Shakira dedicó unas palabras a su colega: "Para mí es un honor y un lujo cantar esta canción que significa tanto para mí con esta mujer tan admirada y tan querida." Tras finalizar el espectáculo, Dua Lipa celebró el encuentro en sus perfiles oficiales, expresando su gratitud hacia la colombiana y remarcando la química y conexión viva que experimentaron junto al público durante la velada.

articles.title: Roman Reigns reveals his leukemia battle is still ongoing years after his WWE return: How leukemia has impacted his workouts, treatment choices and WWE career
articles.summary: Roman Reigns shares insights into his ongoing battle with chronic myeloid leukemia, detailing how it has shaped his training, treatment choices, and WWE career since his return.
articles.body: Roman Reigns has stated his chronic myeloid leukemia remains a health concern years after his return to WWE. It’s something that’s controlled, but it’s something that you have to monitor and be careful with the decisions one makes regarding your recovery, Reigns told Men’s Health.The update also details how his medical history has affected his training and his approach to treatment options. Reigns said he prefers to stick with methods he can control safely rather than try out recovery products and will seek the advice of medical professionals if necessary. has changed for WWE star Roman Reigns since leukemia returnedRoman Reigns is now more cautious in his recovery because of his history of chronic myeloid leukemia and the continued presence of small molecular traces of the disease.Reigns was first diagnosed with leukemia in 2007 and then publicly announced the return of the disease in 2018 when he gave up the WWE Universal Championship and left wrestling to get treatment. He announced he was in remission in February 2019 and eventually made his way back to WWE.But his latest comments make it clear that returning to the ring didn’t mean the health problem was gone altogether. Reigns said his CML is currently under control and below baseline, but he hasn't yet reached the level for molecular remission.Roman Reigns has become more cautious about recoveryThe most obvious practical change seems to be Reigns’ attitude to healing treatments. During the Men’s Health Strong Talk discussion, he was asked about peptides and other methods athletes sometimes look to for recovery.Reigns said his medical history doesn’t allow him to just go experimenting with that stuff. He said he'd heard about peptides, but hadn't used them, adding that anything invasive had risks he wasn't willing to take without proper medical consideration.That caution is especially important for a WWE performer whose career depends on strength, conditioning and physical durability. His training therefore has to balance performance demands with long-term health.Reigns also discussed how his training has changed from simply trying to get as big as he can. In his recent Men’s Health appearance, the WWE star said he’s focusing more on functionality, longevity, and keeping his physical capabilities as he gets older.That philosophy meshes with the demands of his current career. Reigns has shifted his training philosophy away from being physique and performance heavy to one that includes movement, lower body work and takes out unnecessary strain.His past conditioning talks also revealed how health problems affected his conditioning. Rather than trying to stick to the same routine at all costs, Reigns altered his cardio and training regimen during times when leukemia compromised him more.How leukemia has affected Roman Reigns' WWE careerAt several key moments, Reigns’ WWE career has been touched directly by leukemia. One of the biggest disruptions of his career came in 2018 with the diagnosis that led to him vacating the WWE Universal Championship and taking time away from the company.His 2019 return eventually produced one of the defining modern championship runs in WWE, but his latest comments about his health show that the medical battle remains part of his long-term reality.Reigns is the reigning WWE World Heavyweight Champion and is still performing at the top of the professional wrestling world. There have also been reports that he is scheduled to defend the title against LA Knight at WWE Money in the Bank.So the latest update for Reigns is less about leaving WWE and more about how he continues to compete while dealing with a serious medical history. articles.title: Alex Ovechkin's NHL Retirement Decision Revealed in Emotional Video After Historic Capitals Career
articles.summary: Washington Capitals legend Alex Ovechkin announced the 2026-27 season will be his last in the NHL.
articles.body:
Washington Capitals legend Alex Ovechkin announced the 2026-27 season will be his last in the NHL.

The three-time Hart Memorial Trophy winner informed his teammates in the locker room:

In a statement released by the Caps, he said that "I know in my heart it's the right decision."

"It was important for me to make this announcement before our first home game, so I have the chance to thank all the people around the game, everyone who has been so important to me and my family and helped be through good times and tough losses," he said. "I wouldn't have been able to achieve everything I have in my life without them."

Ovechkin is embarking on his 22nd season, and he turned 41 in September. Anyone who follows the NHL knew his exit was coming sooner rather than later.

Still, there's always an initial shock when the uncertain becomes certain.

A 12-time All-Star, Ovechkin is a defining star of his era alongside the Pittsburgh Penguins' Sidney Crosby. His 929 goals are the most in NHL history, and his 759 assists are only three behind Nicklas Bäckström for Washington's all-time mark.

Giving himself a farewell tour will allow Ovechkin's fans and peers to properly celebrate everything he achieved on the ice. It's bound to serve as a source of motivation for the Capitals as well.

The Caps won their opener 5-2 over the Carolina Hurricanes before losing 3-1 to the Tampa Bay Lightning on Saturday. In general, they should be in the thick of the Stanley Cup Playoff hunt.

Coincidentally, Crosby and the Penguins are next up for Washington. The two teams face off Wednesday at Capital One Arena. Ovechkin and Crosby will cross paths three more times after that: Jan. 18, March 13 and April 4.

The last of those encounters is the Capitals' final home game. They close with three straight on the road, wrapping up the year on April 10 against the Philadelphia Flyers.

Ovechkin's swan song could extend beyond that if Washington punches its ticket to the postseason. Regardless, the games he does have left just took on an added significance.

articles.title: Brie Bella Injury Update Timeline to Return from Major Injury Suffered at WWE SummerSlam
articles.summary: After suffering a serious shoulder injury at SummerSlam in August, Brie Bella still faces a long road to recovery.
articles.body:
After suffering a serious shoulder injury at SummerSlam in August, Brie Bella still faces a long road to recovery.

During Monday's episode of The Nikki & Brie Show , Bella revealed that she's been completely limited by her broken scapula, so her timeline to return to the ring is unknown.

"You guys, I have not been able to do cardio. I'm a cardio queen, and so I haven't even been able to run since this injury. So I still think my days to be in-ring are still far, unfortunately," Bella said (h/t Subhojeet Mukherjee of Ringside News). "I am not the type of girl anymore who's gonna rush things. I want all of it out before I make that comeback."

Bella said that she recently underwent a CT scan on her injured shoulder, but she's still awaiting the results.

"I did get nervous… I was like, 'It's because my bones fused?' But he's like, 'No, I don't know.' So he wouldn't tell me anything. But I'm feeling strong, I'm feeling good. I'm still not cleared to do any, you know, the exercises I would like to do," she said. "There are times where I will go to shut a window and I get really bad spasms or sharp pains. I'm still really cautious about picking up things that aren't heavier than five pounds… I'm not cleared to pick up anything heavier than five pounds."

Bella said her current recovery mainly consists of physical therapy with the goal of strengthening the muscles around the scapula. However, even if she gets positive results from her CT scan, she's still a long way from returning to the ring.

"Even if my bones have fused, it doesn't mean I get to go back yet," she said. "It's a very long process when it comes to shoulder/scapula stuff. It just means I get to take the next step to rehabbing."

articles.title: Luke Littler beaten by Cam Crabtree in semi-finals of World Youth Championship
articles.summary: Luke Littler returned to action after his shock defeat in the World Grand Prix; He reached the semi-finals of the World Youth Championship but was unexpectedly beaten by Cam Crabtree; watch Grand Slam of Darts live on Sky Sports from November 14
articles.body:
Crabtree beat Littler 6-5 and will meet Jan Schmidt in the final at Minehead.

Littler came back from 2-0 to level the game, but Crabtree ultimately overhauled him.

Littler was playing for the first time since his shock defeat to Luke Woodhouse in the opening stage of the World Grand Prix.

Crabtree raced into a 2-0 lead against 2023 World Youth Champion Littler, but the sport's premier player soon regained control with a brutal three-leg spell.

The Warrington sensation followed up a magnificent 164 checkout with back-to-back 14-darters to move 3-2 ahead, but Crabtree was undeterred, hitting back with 92 and 100 finishes to take a 5-4 lead.

Littler responded with a terrific 117 to force a last-leg decider, although Crabtree wasn't to be denied, firing in a 16-dart hold on double six to prevail with a 97.91 average.

Littler had been flawless in the group stage at the World Youth Championship, taking three wins. He then saw off Lewis Cook, but at one point Cook, only 16 years old himself, went 3-0 ahead only for Littler to stage a comeback.

Littler then beat David Fidler 6-1 and reached the quarter-finals after defeating Archie Self 6-4.

Littler took a 6-2 victory over Harrison Leigh to win through to the final four but then came unstuck against the 23-year-old Crabtree.

This tournament is open to players aged 16-24 and offers £60,000 in prize money.

Earlier this year Littler looked like he would steamroll all before him, but his bid for a clean sweep of all major PDC titles in 2026 ended in Amsterdam where the Briton complained about being repeatedly whistled at by Dutch supporters.

A dip in form has then been compounded by unexpected defeats at the World Grand Prix and now the World Youth Championship.

Sky Sports commentator Wayne Mardle questioned why Littler entered the World Youth Championship. "I don't know what he wants to gain from it," he said. "It doesn't make any sense to me.

"I just don't see the value time-wise. Because time-management's everything when you're playing a lot."

Littler's exit from the World Grand Prix could be cause for concern. "I'm never concerned with people losing because this is a hard industry to keep winning. The fact that he was winning all those matches on the trot in majors anyway was ridiculous," Mardle said.

"It was the way he's been losing. He's not been playing that well. This is no offence and no disrespect to Luke Woodhouse. Luke Woodhouse actually said himself that it was a scrappy game.

"It's the fact that Luke Littler didn't play well," Mardle added. "I just think he's underperforming right now, for whatever reason.

"Bearing in mind we're humans, we're not robots, we're not automatons, we do have off days as well. He's just having a couple of off days right now."

articles.title: Luke Littler: World number one knocked out of World Youth Championships in semi-finals
articles.summary: Luke Littler is knocked out of the World Youth Championships in the semi-finals by Cam Crabtree.
articles.body:
Luke Littler missed out on the chance to hold the senior and youth world titles simultaneously after suffering a surprise semi-final defeat at the World Youth Championship.

The 19-year-old world number one was beaten 6-5 by world number 68 Cam Crabtree, who will face German Jan Schmidt in the final on 29 November.

That match will take place on finals day at the Players Championship Finals in Minehead – an event Littler has also yet to qualify for having skipped the majority of Pro Tour events this season.

He is currently ranked 126th in the Players Championship order of merit and only the top 64 qualify.

Four Players Championship events remain, but two of those are in Den Bosch in the Netherlands - where Littler withdrew from events recently after being subjected to boos by the crowds .

Littler has won successive full World Championships and won the youth title as a 16-year-old in 2023, but the semi-final loss to 23-year-old Crabtree was his second successive exit at that stage having lost to Beau Greaves in 2025. He could though enter four more times, with the tournament open to players aged 23 or under at the start of the season.

The loss is the latest in a series of surprise exits for Littler, who was knocked out of the World Grand Prix in the first round by Luke Woodhouse and lost to Jonny Clayton in the quarter-finals of the World Series of Darts finals.

articles.title: B/R's Great 8 Moments and Memories of Alex Ovechkin's NHL Career
articles.summary: Alex Ovechkin officially announced Monday that the 2026-27 NHL season will be his last.
articles.body:
Alex Ovechkin officially announced Monday that the 2026-27 NHL season will be his last.

Ovechkin signed a one-year contract this past summer and turned 41 last month -- it's not like this was unexpected. But the official announcement makes it easier for all of us to enjoy the farewell tour of the best goal scorer of all time.

So as we see if he has one more playoff run and a few more special moments up his sleeve this season, let's reflect on the eight greatest moments and memories of No. 8's career so far.

Alex Ovechkin's rookie season remains one of the best in NHL history, with 52 goals in 81 games and a Calder Trophy to boot.

The biggest highlight-reeler of the bunch was goal No. 32, scored in January 2006 against the Phoenix Coyotes. To this day, this goal ranks among Ovechkin's wildest of all time.

After sliding and falling on his back, Ovechkin was able to remain in control of the puck and slide a backhander past Brian Boucher.

We all knew Ovechkin was going to have a special career from the moment he scored two goals in his NHL debut, but goal No. 32 really solidified that he could become one of the best goal-scorers of all time.

After finishing the 2007-08 season with 65 goals and 112 points, Ovechkin won the Hart Trophy, the Art Ross Trophy, the Rocket Richard Trophy, and the Ted Lindsay Award, given to the most outstanding player as voted by the NHL Players' Association. He became the first player in NHL history to sweep all four of these awards in one season.

As impressive as his goal-scoring will always be, the four-trophy sweep, including the Hart Trophy, showed that his career is about much more than just scoring goals.

If the rivalry between Alex Ovechkin and Sidney Crosby isn't your favorite NHL rivalry of all time, you're lying to yourself if it isn't at least in your top three.

These two joined the league in the same year and ushered in a new era of skill and finesse in the NHL. Not only did both players dominate the league year after year in their primes, but they've continued to perform at an elite level long past their 20s.

They've met in four postseason series (2009, 2016, 2017 won by Pittsburgh; 2018 won by Washington), and every series winner eventually went on to hoist the Stanley Cup.

There are too many iconic moments from twenty years of Ovechkin and Crosby going at it, but the two going hat trick for hat trick in Game 2 of the 2009 Eastern Conference Semifinals is tough to beat.

His Love of Subway Sandwiches, Cheetos and Mamma Lucia's

Most NHL players have their quirks, and Ovechkin's has been a shameless love for junk food. The best goal-scorer in NHL history is fueled by everything from mid-game soda (sugar is fast-burning fuel, after all) to gas station Subway to his pre-game meal from " Mamma Lucia " in the DC area.

What is "Mamma Lucia," you ask? According to Brooks Orpik, it's a chicken parm pasta concoction that Ovechkin will eat even at 9 a.m. if there's a 12 p.m. matinee ahead.

"It's a pasta dish that's like chicken parm with noodles, bread, cheese, the kind of thing you want to take a five-hour nap after eating," Orpik told the Players' Tribune . "He makes a big display of it too. There's no shame. It'll be eleven in the morning, way before anyone is really thinking about eating lunch, and Ovi will walk into the dining area yelling, 'Mamma Lucia! Mamma Lucia!'"

There's something genuinely endearing that in the era of players drinking green smoothies and eating chickpea pasta, one of the greatest to ever do it is still kickin' on a diet like this at 41 years young.

As Ovechkin's career reached the decade mark, his Capitals were right there , making the playoffs and advancing past the first round more often than not. Year after year, though, they fell short of the ultimate goal. Worse yet, they kept failing to beat their rival Penguins along the way. The pressure was at an all-time high leading up to Washington's 2018 championship run.

As agonizing as the buildup to that year had been, it's clear all of the disappointment along the way made Ovechkin's first and only Stanley Cup even sweeter.

The 2018 Stanley Cup was the first in Capitals franchise history; Ovechkin won the Conn Smythe Trophy after recording 27 points in 24 games, and yes, they defeated the Penguins in the second round along the way.

Ovechkin has had one of the most remarkable individual careers in NHL history, but his resume as one of the best hockey players of all time just wouldn't have felt complete without a Stanley Cup.

So, yeah, about that catharsis. When Ovechkin and the Capitals finally got that Stanley Cup monkey off their back, they partied accordingly.

In what still stands as one of the most epic Cup-celebration summers, Ovechkin was all over Washington, having the time of his life. He was jumping into fountains, drinking from the Cup in the stands at Nationals Park, and throwing the entire city into a multi-day public bender.

He earned every second of it, and even the biggest Capitals haters among us had to tip their hats.

When you think about Alex Ovechkin, what's the first thing that comes to mind? For us, it's the position on the ice where he has scored so many goals that it has become known as his office.

There's just nothing like Ovechkin's one-timer from the top left circle. The best players in the world can fully anticipate this shot coming and still remain utterly powerless to stop it.

It's not some rare, out-of-this-world maneuver; it's a standard and popular area to take a shot — especially on the power play. The power and skill behind Ovechkin's shot in his sweet spot are what set him apart and have turned a typical play into such an iconic facet of his career.

It was a feat that seemed almost impossible a decade ago, but as Ovechkin continued to consistently rake in the goals over the years, we thought he might break Wayne Gretzky's all-time goals record.

Then, one fateful day on Long Island (April 6, 2025), the then-39-year-old Ovechkin shoveled a power-play goal past Ilya Sorokin from his trademark spot at the top of the left-wing circle. It was magic goal number 895, surpassing Gretzky's 894.

He's currently sitting at 929 goals as he starts his final season, so let's see how far he can take the record now that he owns it.

articles.title: Super-subs help France demolish Belgium with late flurry
articles.summary: Michael Olise scores twice and assists as France come from 1-0 with 13 minutes left to beat Belgium 4-1
articles.body:
France came from a goal down to beat Belgium 4-1 in their Nations League Group A1 meeting at the Stade de France on Monday.

Zinedine Zidane secured his first home win in charge, three days after a 1-1 draw against Italy, thanks to his substitutes.

Belgium’s Dodi Lukebakio put the visitors ahead in the 35th minute, but Desire Doue, Rayan Cherki and Michael Olise, all on the bench at kickoff, turned the match on its head in the final 15 minutes.

Doue levelled with a left-footed shot from the edge of the box in the 77th minute. Four minutes later, Cherki put his side in front, finishing from an Olise cross.

Olise then completed a brace just before and during stoppage time, the second latching onto Doue’s slick pass after a clinical break.

In the same Nations League group, Italy secured a 3-1 victory over Turkiye with Gianluca Scamacca, Riccardo Calafiori and Pio Esposito scoring. Turkiye’s Aral Simsir had equalised earlier, just after the hour mark.

France sit top of Group A1 with 10 points, three ahead of Italy and four clear of Belgium. Turkiye are at the bottom with four defeats from four matches.

France head to Milan to face the Azzurri in their penultimate group game next month before hosting Turkiye.

articles.title: SEC coach: ‘I think everyone is disappointed when they play Alabama right now’
articles.summary: Since the loss to the Tide, this SEC school has been on the roll.
articles.body:
Kentucky coach Will Stein, who had just led his team to a dramatic come-from-behind overtime win over South Carolina, was asked Saturday how his team rebounded since a loss to Alabama.

"I mean I think everyone is disappointed when they play Alabama right now," Stein told the SEC Network. "They score consistently on everybody."

Last month, the Tide trailed the Wildcats just 17-13 in the first half before Kalen DeBoer's team scored 32 unanswered in the 45-17 win. Since then, Kentucky has reeled off three straight wins.

Alabama, meanwhile, remains undefeated and has climbed to No. 6 in the latest Associated Press poll, while averaging more than 49 points a game.

Also, make sure to visit our college football prediction markets guide if you're interested in learning more about how to bet on college football.

Perhaps no Kentucky win was more dramatic than Saturday when Stein held up two fingers on the sidelines after his team's overtime touchdown, letting the Wildcats know his intention to end things right away.

Strong safety Ty Bryant hinted he knew his coach's intentions a few days earlier. Bryant, a senior, usually sits in on staff meetings late in the week. "I'm not going to tell you what (Stein) said," Bryant continued. "He's aggressive. I'm good with that."

So were all connected with No. 24 Kentucky (4-1, 2-1 Southeastern Conference) after Kenny Minchey's 6-yard TD pass to Henry Boyer and successful 2-point pass to Willie Rodriguez at the back of the end zone gave the Wildcats a 35-34 OT win at South Carolina after trailing 17-0.

"We just felt the momentum South Carolina had taken at the end of regulation," Stein said. "We needed to go for two. That's what we did. Felt really confident about the play call and executed it well."

Kentucky's players celebrated, spilling onto the field after a second major road win for first-year coach Stein, who's team beat then-ninth-ranked Texas A&M 31-21 at College Station two weeks ago.

And now, Kentucky gets to dream of even bigger things and a special season in Stein's debut when it faces No. 11 LSU at home next Saturday.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Monday Internationals Update: Penalty Save from Mamardashvili, Injury Worry for Jacquet
articles.summary: Largely a quiet day on the international front
articles.body:
The main headline for Monday's internationals action is the penalty save (and additional clean sheet) for Giorgi Mamardashvili as Georgia drew 0-0 with Northern Ireland. The Liverpool backup keeper was among Georgia's strongest players, making five saves across the match (his side only managed to challenge Northern Ireland with two shots on target, meanwhile).

Elsewhere Liverpool senior players got a few minutes on the board with their national sides, with Dominik Szoboszlai captaining Hungary in their 2-1 win against Ukraine with Miloš Kerkez suspended and thus not involved. On-loan Ármin Pécsi was on the bench as a back-up goalkeeper.

Bradley Barcola started and played 72 minutes for France, though his side's late comeback occurred after he was subbed off: France was 1-0 down to Belgium until Désiré Doué opened scoring for the French in the 77th minute, and it eventually escalated wildly into a 4-1 win for France. Barcola played well without necessarily generating a lot of highlights. Perhaps worryingly Jérémy Jacquet was forced out of a start for France with what was deemed a "little" injury, though the hope is that his rest was to preserve fitness rather than due to a true fitness issue. Given the strength of his performances thus far it's very worrying that the young defender was not in the squad against Belgium.

articles.title: Chiefs' Thornton out 12-16 weeks after dislocating left ankle and tearing ligaments, AP source says
articles.summary: Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton is expected to miss 12 to 16 weeks after dislocating his left ankle and tearing ligaments in it, a person with knowledge...
articles.body:
Chiefs wide receiver Tyquan Thornton is expected to miss 12 to 16 weeks after dislocating his left ankle and tearing ligaments in it, a person with knowledge of the injury told The Associated Press on Monday.

The person, who spoke on condition of anonymity because the team hadn't announced the details, said Thornton will have surgery this week.

Thornton was having the best game of his career when he got hurt at the end of a 55-yard catch during Kansas City's 30-27 victory over Las Vegas . His ankle got caught beneath him and twisted at a gruesome angle after he was hauled down from behind. Thornton briefly stood up to celebrate and signal first down before going to the ground and being carted off the field .

He had five catches for 111 yards and two touchdowns from Patrick Mahomes.

The undefeated Chiefs (4-0) also lost wideout Rashee Rice earlier in the game to a hamstring injury. They have a bye this weekend.

Thornton was a second-round pick by New England in 2022 but never had more than 22 catches. He joined the Chiefs last season and had a career-best 438 yards receiving on only 19 receptions for an average of 19.9 yards per catch.

He had 11 catches for 219 yards and two scores this season.

articles.title: Buffalo Bills' Josh Allen-led offense takes a sloppy step back in loss after season-opening surge
articles.summary: (AP) — Upon opening the season with two potent offensive performances, Buffalo Bills coach Joe Brady had a forceful response when asked if the Josh Allen-led...
articles.body:
ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. (AP) — Upon opening the season with two potent offensive performances, Buffalo Bills coach Joe Brady had a forceful response when asked if the Josh Allen-led production was sustainable.

"With the crew we have, I'm (unhappy) every time we don't (score a touchdown), if I'm being honest," the first-year coach said. "And that's not cocky."

Two outings later have provided a much different picture.

Buffalo's offense hasn't so much dried up in splitting the past two games, including a 29-26 loss to New England on Sunday.

Rather, it's shown signs of sputtering and being impeded by ball-security issues.

The Bills' four punts on Sunday were one fewer than they combined for in the first three weeks. Buffalo also went three-and-out three times against New England, after doing so just once before this season.

And after opening with two turnover-free outings, the Bills have seven giveaways (three interceptions, four lost fumbles) since, with Allen's late-game interception — an ill-advised underthrown deep ball into double coverage on second down — sealing the loss against the Patriots.

This is not the formula for success for any team, never mind the Bills, who have been required to lean more on offense to compensate for a new-look defense experiencing growing-pain issues and depleted by injuries.

Though it's easy to pin the blame on the defense, something that became common during Sean McDermott's final years as coach and led to his firing in January, the offense bears its share.

Brady, on Sunday, blamed himself by saying he needs to be a better offensive play-caller.

Allen, meantime, spread the blame by saying it's on all three phases: "Offense, defense, special teams, everybody. We all feel like we could play better," he said.

That might be true. But Allen and Brady's aggressive approach to offense might not be helping.

Brady's strategy to take the ball first when winning the coin flip didn't pan out. Buffalo went three-and-out to open the game and had to wait seven minutes to get the ball back after the defense allowed a 12-play, 97-yard TD drive.

For all the defense's deficiencies, the unit did force three straight punts in the second half after Buffalo fell behind 21-17 to open the third quarter. And then there was Allen's game-ending interception, which he acknowledged being a mistake.

If McDermott was occasionally criticized for supposedly holding back the offense, he did so with a vision of Buffalo playing complementary football.

Entering Sunday, the Bills were 50-5 at home and had won 19 straight when leading in the fourth quarter during Allen's eight-plus seasons. They hadn't lost in that situation since a 24-22 defeat against Denver on Nov. 13, 2023.

The outcome led to McDermott firing offensive coordinator Ken Dorsey and promoting his quarterbacks coach, Brady, who is now the one in charge.

Third down conversions. The Bills have converted at least 50% of their third down situations in each of the past three outings, including going 6 of 12 against New England. Buffalo is a combined 21 of 36 over that span.

Fourth down stops. Though the Bills defense is a respectable 22 of 54 in third down situations, the unit has allowed opponents to go 6 of 7 on fourth down.

WR Keon Coleman . The third-year receiver, who was questioned by team owner Terry Pegula in January, had six catches for a team-leading 116 yards and a touchdown. It was his second-best outing in yards, and came in an outing Buffalo's top threat, DJ Moore, was sidelined by a shoulder injury in the first half.

CB Max Hairston. The second-year player struggled in taking over the No. 1 role with Christian Benford sidelined by a toe injury. Hairston was beaten on both of Romeo Doubs' TD catches, and was late to tackle TE Hunter Henry completing a 12-yard catch-and-run on third-and-10 in allowing New England to run out the final 49 seconds.

Moore aggravated an injury he first sustained in Week 2. DT Ed Oliver did not return after hurting his knee in the second half. Third CB Dee Alford was sidelined by an ankle injury. Practice squad call-up CB Te'Cory Couch hurt his hamstring.

66-9 — Buffalo's record under Allen when leading after the half, after blowing a 13-10 edge on Sunday.

Have an extra day to regroup before heading west to face the Los Angeles Rams on Monday. The Bills will stay in Southern California next week before traveling to play the Las Vegas Raiders on Oct. 18.

articles.title: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns says getting an extension before the season begins doesn't look good
articles.summary: PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday the prospects of him getting a contract extension with the reigning NBA-champion New York Knicks before th...
articles.body:
PHILADELPHIA (AP) — Karl-Anthony Towns said Monday the prospects of him getting a contract extension with the reigning NBA-champion New York Knicks before the start of the regular season were not looking good.

Opening night against the 76ers and the Knicks' banner-raising celebration on Oct. 20 is a little over two weeks away.

Towns, who is set to turn 31 on Nov. 15, is eligible for a four-year, $276 million deal. He is due to make $57 million this season and has a $61.1 million player option for 2027-28.

Asked at the start of training camp how he would feel about negotiations extending into the season, Towns said, "In this situation, there's no comfortability to be had."

Towns is a six-time All-Star who averaged nearly 16 points and had more than 10 rebounds a game during the Knicks' first title run since 1973. He believes he should be rewarded for his role in winning it all.

"I want to do something that can keep the team together and work with the Knicks and also values me," Towns told reporters before the Knicks' preseason opener at Philadelphia.

Owner James Dolan has said the team would not go into the second spending apron. Big man Mitchell Robinson left New York after eight seasons to sign a three-year deal in free agency with rival Boston.

articles.title: Murray and the Vikings might've found some momentum for a lagging offense, late in their latest win
articles.summary: (AP) — The unbeaten Minnesota Vikings won another game behind a suffocating defense and sterling special teams, while their offense remained disjointed and u...
articles.body:
EAGAN, Minn. (AP) — The unbeaten Minnesota Vikings won another game behind a suffocating defense and sterling special teams , while their offense remained disjointed and uninspiring for a restless home crowd.

Lost in the din of another grind-it-out win and the mild booing sparked by a series of stalled possessions, however, was a promising fourth-quarter performance by Kyler Murray when the Vikings needed their passing attack the most.

Perhaps that was a sign the offense will be just fine with more time. Maybe it'll prove to be a mirage. More likely, the results over the remainder of the season will land somewhere in the middle. Nonetheless, Murray and his teammates gained some vital steam with their finish against Miami on Sunday that gave the Vikings a 4-0 record.

After completing 12 of 13 passes for 112 yards in the fourth quarter of the 15-10 victory, helping the Vikings get eight first downs and hold the ball for 14 of 15 minutes, Murray said he felt "present" in a way he hadn't experienced yet with his new club.

"I definitely felt like the game was moving slower," Murray said. "I was a little more in control, not perfect by any means, but to be able to get that many reps like I did today, play four quarters again, see defenses, see coverages, see guys moving around and getting to the field zones in man coverages, all that, you can't put a price tag on that playing this position. I think we're only going to get better."

Murray went 27 of 37 for 249 yards, including six throwaways and three drops by intended receivers. The combination of the game-long commitment by the Dolphins to playing split-safety coverage and the absence of star Justin Jefferson made the intermediate and deep passes more difficult. Murray repeatedly held the ball in the pocket too long, taking four sacks against a team that had none over the first three games.

But he leaned hard on tight end T.J. Hockenson and connected with Jordan Addison for a crucial 27-yard gain on a tough throw to an in-cutting route at midfield with about four minutes left.

"I thought it said a lot about Kyler and the group as a whole, fighting through some adversity there," coach Kevin O'Connell said.

Murray's preseason work on a demanding playbook was affected some by the competition with J.J. McCarthy , limiting his turns with the first team until he was announced as the starter on Aug. 11.

Then he was sidelined in the first quarter of his debut by a concussion that kept him out the following week, too. In Murray's return, Jefferson had an injury force an early exit. The duo has played only 18 snaps together through four games.

The Vikings, not coincidentally, are the only team in the last 90 years, according to Sportradar data, to start a season 4-0 and have at least two games with no offensive touchdowns.

"There's no lack of confidence by any means," Murray said. "Obviously we've got to be better and cleaner, and we will be."

The pass defense was in prime form against the Dolphins, limiting Malik Willis to nine completions in 17 attempts. The Vikings lead the NFL in sacks per pass attempt and rank fourth in yards allowed per pass play.

The Vikings, on the flip side, are second-worst in the league in sacks allowed per pass attempt. Protection, decision-making and play-calling are all factors.

Hockenson tied his career high with 13 receptions for 119 yards, his fifth career game with a 100% catch rate. Eight of his receptions went for first downs, and he picked up more blocking responsibility, too, after fellow tight end Josh Oliver suffered a torn biceps that likely ended his season. With his fourth 100-yard game for the Vikings, Hockenson tied Joe Senser for most by a tight end in team history.

With rookie Brett Thorson out for a second straight game because of a hamstring injury, veteran Johnny Hekker had punts that grossed only 31 and 20 yards.

The Vikings got some bad news Monday on left guard Donovan Jackson , who likely will miss the rest of the regular season with a knee injury. Left tackle Christian Darrisaw is in the concussion protocol and uncertain for this week, along with Jefferson and his sprained ankle.

26.1 — The percentage of opponent possessions against the Vikings that have resulted in points, the best rate in the league.

The Vikings play this week at New Orleans, where a noisy stadium could pose a problem with their susceptibility to pre-snap penalties. The offense had five of them against Miami, including an illegal formation call that negated a 21-yard pass from Murray to Addison in the first quarter.

articles.title: Pacers’ Kelly Oubre Jr. Causing Excitement For 2026-27
articles.summary: After Kelly Oubre Jr. joined the Indiana Pacers this offseason, he was expected to have an impact. As the season nears, excitement has grown around his role...
articles.body:
After Kelly Oubre Jr. joined the Indiana Pacers this offseason, he was expected to have an impact. As the season nears, excitement has grown around his role on the team. The versatile forward and guard is replacing Bennedict Mathurin 's role on the team and has the potential to be an extremely important player in the Pacers' rotation this season.

Oubre is expected to be an essential piece to the Pacers' game plans and will come off the bench for most games. The longtime veteran will bring experience, versatility, and athleticism to the team. Recently, Oubre has shared some encouraging things about the Pacers that have created more excitement about the team in general. Oubre has also stood out early on with the Pacers, building extra anticipation and hope over his performance this season.

During the Pacers' FanJam, their annual team scrimmage to tip off the NBA season, Oubre dropped 17 points in ten minutes, shooting 7/10 during his time on the court. While the exhibition match is not very serious and is a fun event for fans, Oubre made an impact early on with his new team, which is an encouraging sign.

Kelly Oubre Jr. Drawing Encouraging Reports Early In Training Camp

Head Coach Rick Carlisle has already been impressed by Oubre and has spoken highly about what he is seeing out of him. When speaking to the media about training camp, Carlisle said, " [Kelly Oubre Jr.] had a large impact on practice today on both ends. He shot the ball really well. Defensively, he's sticky, he's tough, he's difficult to screen, and he's an edgy competitor. So it's exactly what we need. " Oubre is the right fit for the Pacers , and Carlisle's compliments of him show he fits well in the Pacers' system.

Indiana's roster is full of fast, physical, and athletic players who are versatile on both sides of the ball. Oubre shouldn't have any trouble adjusting to the Pacers' play style, as he will be surrounded by competitive teammates like him.

During the Pacers 2026-27 media day , Oubre got a chance to talk to reporters. Oubre said that the major draw that eventually brought him to ink a deal with the Pacers was the team culture. Oubre said he did not need to hear a pitch about the team or be told about the culture; he could already see how the team operated, its strong leadership, and the culture that has been sustained in Indiana. Oubre saying this compliments the culture that has been built within the organization and shows how the team leaders have built relationships within the team to make the Pacers organization a team players want to be a part of.

While Indiana is still early in training camp, Oubre has already drawn very encouraging reports from the media, coaches, and players. By making an impact early, excitement around Oubre's role on the team continues to grow. Oubre will be a great addition on and off the court for the Pacers and can make a huge impact on the team this season.

Oubre's acknowledgement of the Pacers' culture speaks volumes about how the team operates as well, which gives fans more hope for the upcoming season. The NBA is sleeping on the Pacers , and with the addition of players like Oubre combined with the healthy culture of the team, Indiana could come and surprise anyone who has overlooked them. As the season draws closer, the Pacers are becoming an exciting team to watch, and their attempt to return to the Finals after a disappointing season without Tyrese Haliburton will be a fun storyline to pay attention to.

articles.title: Why does Texas A&M's Mike Elko want his team to feel joy, not relief, after winning a game?
articles.summary: After two straight SEC losses, Texas A&M beat Arkansas 34-7. Elko says blocking out outside opinions helps his team enjoy the win.
articles.body:
COLLEGE STATION - Texas A&M coach Mike Elko doesn't want to feel relief after winning a football game.

"The day I feel relief for winning is the day I quit," Elko said Saturday after his Aggies beat Arkansas . "We have joy when we win. That's the word that we use when we win football games."

But why joy? Why is that the emotion he wants his team to feel?

"Because that means we're not listening to you guys, if I'm being honest," Elko said Monday during his weekly media availability. "And when I say you guys, I just mean the noise."

In Elko's mind, relief is an emotion that comes as a result of listening to the outside noise. He doesn't want his team listening to anybody not in the locker room, so feeling relief after a win would mean the team is paying mind to the detractors - whether it's in the traditional media, on social media or anywhere else people are expressing their opinions.

Relief would also be the result of anticipating positivity from outsiders, something Elko doesn't care enough to worry about.

"When you start talking about words like relief, the relief would come because we're not going to hear bad things from you. That's what relief would be from," Elko explained, again using you as a catch-all term. "Joy would be because together we collectively accomplished something that we set out to do, and so we're going to celebrate that with joy with each other because that's all that matters is each other."

The outside noise has been loud this season, although that's par for the course at a school like Texas A&M with passionate fans, a large alumni base and high expectations. Two straight losses to start conference play, a home loss to unranked Kentucky and a blowout road defeat to LSU, crescendoed the noise like a conductor directing an orchestra during a symphony.

The Aggies often talk about isolating themselves from the noise, Elko said. Social media has changed how they approach doing so, but teams have always been fighting against the noise.

"It's just how you have to manage the modern athlete, and I don't think there's anything wrong with it," Elko said. "I don't think it's good, bad, whatever. It's just part of society today. It's just a part of mentally preparing your kids to go out and play at the level they're capable of. There's always been a motivational, mental side of the game. I think social media is just a big piece of that nowadays."

Texas A&M has another chance to celebrate with joy Saturday in Columbia, Mo., with its matchup against No. 14 Missouri. The Tigers are entering on a high after a major upset victory over Florida, who were ranked at No. 8. It would be the Aggies' first win against a ranked opponent and on the road this season.

Coming off the 34-7 win over the Razorbacks, Elko said the team has increased confidence.

"When you win, things are better," Elko said. "I don't think there's any dispute behind that. I don't know that we ever stopped working, but you definitely feel mojo. You feel confidence. You feel more positive vibes in and around it when you win."

articles.title: Not much has been special about Texas' special teams, but Oklahoma may help fix slow start
articles.summary: This season, special teams for Texas football have been anything but special. Will that change against Oklahoma in Saturday's Red River Rivalry matchup?
articles.body:
Special teams have been anything but special this season for Texas football .

Through four games, No. 1 Texas (4-0, 1-0 SEC) is still waiting for that big return on a punt or kickoff. New kicker Gianni Spetic provided a clutch extra point against Ohio State , but he hasn't yet made a pressure field goal.

The Longhorns' struggles on special teams were best illustrated in the team's last game against Tennessee. Texas remained undefeated with a 20-17 win in Knoxville on Sept. 26, but a handful of special teams blunders kept the Volunteers in the game:

• Spetic averaged 61.8 yards per kickoff and had as many of his five kicks go out of bounds as they did for a touchback (one).

• Texas allowed a 57-yard punt return for a touchdown. A UT opponent hadn't scored off a punt return since 2013.

• Texas had a long punt return by freshman Jermaine Bishop Jr. waived off when it was determined that fellow returner Ryan Niblett had signaled for a fair catch.

• Tennessee also recovered an onside kick in the final minutes that set up a failed heave into the end zone on the game's final play. Yes, the SEC later acknowledged that Tennessee should have been penalized for how they set up the onside try. But that mea culpa overshadowed the fact that Texas receiver Ryan Wingo had a chance to land on the ball but couldn't.

"I messed up, (but the defense) came out there and got a stop," Wingo said.

Texas looks for more depth instead of highlights on special teams

During last week's bye, Texas coach Steve Sarkisian recognized his team is having issues on special teams. He seemed less concerned about the Jeff Banks-coached unit's lack of a big return or big kick, though.

Sarkisian instead stressed that the Longhorns must develop more depth on special teams. Through four games, defensive starters Kade Phillips, Graceson Littleton, Justin Cryer and Rasheem Biles have all logged at least 30 special teams snaps.

"The biggest thing on special teams we need to get is we need more depth," Sarkisian said. "We need other guys taking some of the heat off these guys on punt, punt return, kickoff coverage, and so we need the depth to step up. I think that's where we need to place an emphasis on (is) who can we count on to be in those positions to play on special teams to take the load off of those guys so that they can keep being the players that they are on defense."

Longhorns have history of big plays on special teams vs OU

If Texas is going to break out of its special teams funk, Saturday's Red River Rivalry game may be the day to do it. After all, Oklahoma (2-2, 0-1) has been the opposing end of a handful of highlights for UT special teams.

The Red River Rivalry game is where Jordan Shipley scored on a kickoff return during a top-five showdown in 2008 and where Cameron Dicker inserted himself into Longhorns lore with a nod of his head and a 40-yard kick in 2018 . The longest punt return in Longhorns history? Bo Hilliard's 95-yarder against OU in 1932. The longest kickoff return in UT history? Fozzy Whittaker recorded one of the program's five 100-yard returns in the 2011 Red River Rivalry game. The per-punt average of 55.0 that Michael Dickson recorded against the Sooners during his 2017 Ray Guy Award-winning season remains a school record.

Last October, Niblett's 75-yard punt return touchdown broke open a close game. Nearly one year after that 23-6 win over the Sooners, he is confident that big plays are coming for Texas.

"For sure," Niblett said last month. "Heading into SEC play, I feel like we're going to have a good game plan ahead of us."

articles.title: Jake Ferguson’s fourth-down catch kept Dallas’ comeback alive
articles.summary: So much happened on Sunday, but Jake Ferguson had one of the most clutch moments.
articles.body:
Football is all about momentum. Sometimes those shifts happen quickly and unexpectedly. It was CeeDee Lamb who delivered the winning touchdown, but it was Jake Ferguson's crucial catch that made sure the Cowboys still had a chance to score it. It was a real turning point in the game.

With Dallas trailing Houston 30-27 late in the fourth quarter, the comeback was hanging by the smallest of threads. The Cowboys faced fourth-and-4 at their own 32-yard line with 1:34 remaining. Dak Prescott found Ferguson over the middle for seven yards, moving the chains and keeping alive the possession that would decide Sunday's 34-30 victory.

It was a modest gain at the time but as it turned out it held enormous importance. Dallas needed four yards to continue fighting, and Dak trusted his tight end to deliver. Ferguson secured the pass with a sliding catch, giving the offense another set of downs when an incompletion would have handed Houston possession deep in Cowboys territory to kill the game.

That is the moment that stands out in a game filled with swings. Houston had an opportunity to take control of the closing stages. Instead, Dallas kept the ball and could continue attacking. The Cowboys still had plenty of work ahead, but Ferguson's catch allowed everything that followed to happen.

Earlier, there had been little suggestion that Dallas would win. The Cowboys trailed 16-6 at halftime after a frustrating first two quarters. However, KaVontae Turpin's 48-yard return at the start of the second half lifted the team, and Javonte Williams scored an eight-yard touchdown to finish the possession. Houston responded, forcing Dallas to keep chasing.

The Cowboys' offense eventually found consistency, scoring three rushing touchdowns from Williams. Prescott continued to find success with Lamb, leading Dallas to take the lead. However, Houston responded with Woody Marks' late touchdown run, forcing the Cowboys to respond once again. This time, they delivered, securing the victory.

After Ferguson extended the final possession, Prescott advanced Dallas downfield. Completions of 15 yards to Lamb and 22 yards to George Pickens positioned the Cowboys for a scoring opportunity. With 40 seconds left, Prescott connected with Lamb for the winning touchdown, capping off an impressive afternoon for the receiver, who caught 17 passes for 189 yards.

The winning drive covered 74 yards in just 11 plays, showcasing the significant improvement in the offense after halftime. Quarterback Prescott completed 20 of his 25 second-half attempts for 248 yards and a touchdown, providing Brian Schottenheimer's team with the production they needed to overcome their poor start.

Schottenheimer should be commended for assisting the offense in discovering solutions after halftime, and the players should be acknowledged for performing under pressure. A comeback involves more than just a successful adjustment or a motivational talk at halftime. Ultimately, someone must make a crucial play when there's no margin for error, and Ferguson did precisely that.

articles.title: Seahawks sign veteran RB Joe Mixon to practice squad
articles.summary: The Seattle Seahawks are signing veteran running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after he visited and worked out with the team today.
articles.body:
The Seattle Seahawks are signing veteran running back Joe Mixon to their practice squad after he visited and worked out with the team today. Mike Macdonald confirmed reports shortly after 3 p.m. PDT.

Jordan Schultz was first on the news. He also reported that Mixon will wear No. 25 for the Seahawks.

Mixon visited the Seahawks today after Jay Glazer reported the two were in communication yesterday . Since today is the day after the team's Week 4 game against the Los Angeles Chargers, they were able to work the free agent out before they begin their week of practice tomorrow.

Mixon hasn't played since 2024, but was one of the NFL's premier every-down workhorse RBs for the bulk of his career. By choosing to put him on the practice squad, the Seahawks are saying that they want him in the building, but he might still need to shake off some rust. There should be zero expectations from him until we see him on the field for the first time in nearly two years. He has enough experience to adapt quickly and could be elevated to the active roster in Week 5 against the San Francisco 49ers, but it's unrealistic to assume he'll look like the same Pro Bowl-cailber runner.

articles.title: Dublin Jerome, Olentangy Orange girls golfers clinch state berths
articles.summary: Dublin Jerome won the Division I girls golf district title Oct. 5. Olentangy Orange also advanced to state, and Olentangy's Jodie Han was medalist.
articles.body:
ALEXANDRIA – Without compromising his cybersecurity, Olentangy Orange girls golf coach Todd Helline admitted that "2027" is part of almost all of his online passwords because he expected that to be the year his team peaked.

Helline was as quick to acknowledge that a Division I district runner-up finish Oct. 5 at Links at Echo Springs, nine shots behind defending state champion Dublin Jerome , was both a pleasant surprise and especially sweet given that the Pioneers' season ended at this stage a year ago.

Led by sophomore Amelia Buettner 's runner-up finish (71) and a third-place, even-par effort from classmate Amelia Ricker (72), Orange secured a state berth for the first time since 2018.

"The fact that we're here a year early is pretty awesome," Helline said. "When I first took over six years ago, I knew what we had in the pipeline and thought next year would be where everything starts. We made a good run at state last year, and this year I knew we were really good and had a chance, but this is special.

"Early on, most everyone had three-putts. It was a tough start, but once we get our groove, then we feel pretty good. If we are within five or six shots after eight holes, I feel pretty good."

Orange junior Maddie Patton tied for 25th (83) and classmate Ellie Bach tied for 34th (87).

The top two teams and top two individuals not on qualifying teams advanced to state Oct. 12 and 13 at NCR Country Club's North Course in Kettering.

Olentangy junior Jodie Han cruised to a repeat individual championship , shooting a 66 to best Buettner by five shots.

Junior Mallory Quickel's 73 (tied for fourth) led Jerome, which got four rounds in the 70s and steadily pulled away throughout the back nine to win its second district title in three seasons.

"I feel really good about how I responded with the conditions and the wind; it changed directions a lot so you had to be constantly adapting," Quickel said. "It really means a lot to win this after falling short last year [finishing second to Olentangy]. Our depth definitely helps. If you make a mistake, you have a girl to pick up back up."

Junior Nikitha Suresh finished sixth (75), followed by classmate Adella Pawlowski (12th, 77) and freshman Hebe Li (15th, 79).

"They might go through the round giggling and smiling, but they want to rip your heart out," Jerome coach CD Butcher said. "They are just competitors. We weren't playing really well; we were right there with a few teams for a while … other teams were playing well, but we didn't let them get a chance because we just finished the rounds. They just find a way to finish rounds."

Olentangy was third (320), followed by Upper Arlington (325), Granville (326), Olentangy Berlin (338), Dublin Coffman (351), Big Walnut (353), Watterson (358), Olentangy Liberty (381) and Grove City (383).

Olentangy's Han, Upper Arlington's Emerson earn state berths

Han's day was highlighted by an eagle on the par-4 No. 8, capped by a 25-foot putt that helped her stay well clear of a scrum for the second individual berth.

Han finished with four birdies and 10 pars, eight of which came in her final 10 holes.

Han missed the first round of state last year because of an amateur event in Texas but shot a 69 on the final day. She said she is competing in both rounds next week.

"It just felt like every so often, I had a couple good holes and then those added up [without] a ton of bad holes," Han said. "I was just pretty confident over the ball and that's why I made a lot of putts."

Upper Arlington sophomore Eva Emerson tied for fourth (73) and earned the other individual berth, edging four golfers by two shots.

Emerson bogeyed No. 18 and had to wait about 45 minutes to see whether she would advance.

"I had a good bunker shot out and didn't make the putt; I hadn't been checking the scores, so I thought that putt was for me to make it," Emerson said. "Last year I missed state by one stroke and I thought it would happen again."
